thread.title: Overnight Markets: Dow, S&P 500 suffer worst one-day fall in five months

title: Overnight Markets: Dow, S&P 500 suffer worst one-day fall in five months
text:
By Himanshu Singh 30 Jan, 2018 at 02:18 
US stocks retreated from record highs on Monday, with the Dow and the S&P 500 indexes registering their biggest one-day percentage declines in about five months, pulled down by a slide in Apple stocks. 
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 177 points, or 0.67%, to 26,439, the S&P 500 lost 19 points, or 0.67%, to 2,854 and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 39 points, or 0.52%, to 7,467. 
Technology stocks, the biggest gainers in 2017, accounted for much of the slide. Energy companies also fell as crude oil prices finished lower. Utilities and other rate-sensitive sectors declined as bond yields hit their highest level in almost four years. 
Apple (AAPL.O) declined 2.1% on news that the company will halve production of its $999 iPhone X smartphone. The company is due to report earnings on Thursday. 
It was a rocky start to an action-packed week, which will feature U.S. President Donald Trump’s first official State of the Union speech late Tuesday. 
Also ahead this week is the Federal Reserve’s meeting, the U.S. employment report and earnings from a host of high-profile names including Amazon.com (AMZN.O), Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Facebook (FB.O). 
The S&P technology index lost 0.9% and was the biggest drag on the benchmark index following Wall Street’s strongest four-week run since 2016. 
Telecom stocks also slipped on reports that the US government was considering building a 5G wireless network to guard against spying. 
AT&T (T.N) was down 1.5%, Verizon (VZ.N) slipped 1.1% and Sprint (S.N) pulled back by 1.9%. 
Dr Pepper Snapple Group (DPS.N) surged to an all-time high after K-cup maker Keurig Green Mountain said it will acquire the company in a deal worth more than $21 billion. The stock closed up 22.4%. 
In Asia, shares traded moderately lower early on Tuesday, tracking declines seen on Wall Street in the previous session. 
Tokyo's benchmark Nikkei 225 index traded lower by 0.51% in the early going. Over in Seoul, the Kospi edged lower by 0.29% after rising nearly 1% to notch a record close in the previous session. Down Under, the S&P/ASX 200 was lower by 0.66%. 
In Greater China, the Hang Seng Index was down 0.14%, while in Mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index dined 0.15%.
